evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

source: Entropy measures the degree of uncertainty inherent in the distribution of the flies in the behavior space.

claim: When the red light was off, flies exhibited a range of different behaviors, resulting in high entropy.
source: When the red light was off, flies exhibited a range of different behaviors, and the probability that they performed any one behavior was low. This resulted in a low probability density distributed throughout the behavior space and correspondingly high entropy (Figure 2A).

claim: Upon red light activation, the experimental fly line engaged in red light triggered behaviors at the expense of other natural behaviors, generating a drop in entropy.
source: Upon red light activation, the experimental fly line engaged in red light triggered behaviors at the expense of other natural behaviors. This increased the probability that a small region within the behavior space showed a relatively high density, generating a drop in entropy whose timing and duration mirrored that of the red light triggered behaviors (Figure 2A, Video 7).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data analysis.

source: While there are to date no published examples of a single descending neuron triggering different context-dependent behaviors, there are multiple cases in which descending neurons exhibit different physiological responses depending on the state of the animal (e.g. walking, flying, courting, etc.) (Olberg, 1983; Strausfeld and Bassemir, 1985; Olberg and Willis, 1990; Böhm and Schildberger, 1992; Staudacher and Schildberger, 1998; Hedwig, 2000; Staudacher, 2001; Zorović and Hedwig, 2011).
